newsitem.title: USA: Hydro-Quebec seeks U.S. power marketing license.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec seeks U.S. power marketing license.

text.p: Canada's Hydro-Quebec said Friday its U.S. subsidiary HQ Energy Services has applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in Washington for a license to market wholesale electricity in the U.S.
"If FERC grants HQ Energy the license, it would allow us to sell power at market-based prices rather than cost-based prices," said Hydro-Quebec spokeswoman Janet Murphy.
Hydro-Quebec's request, filed Wednesday, coincided with neighboring Ontario Hydro's own filing for permission to market bulk electricity in the U.S. this week.
Both Canadian utilities made their requests well before the mandated January 1, 1998, start of open wholesale electricity competition in the U.S.
Hydro-Quebec said it expected quick approval of its request. "One to two months. It's on a really fast track," Murphy said.

To be allowed to sell power in the U.S. at market prices, Hydro-Quebec must open its own system to competition from power providers in U.S. and Canada. The Quebec government announced in November it plans to do just that.
"The reciprocity is to allow companies outside of Quebec to transmit power through our system," Murphy said.
Hydro-Quebec, with its massive hydro-electric system, has been selling power mainly into New York and New England.
